case.based_on: work/ramp_interp/ RAMP-interpolation formulation on the same 60x32x24 canonical grid used by the earlier grey-candidate test; body-fitted qualification profile identical to work/stage_sv_qualified_laminar

opt_q100_step2_try0_r12.role: disqualified at all three grids on checkMesh

decision: Three binarized (RAMP-penalized, single-Python-owned-projection) Stage T candidates were run through the same qualified Stage V pipeline (checkMesh, explicit residualControl, force stationarity as hard gates) used for the earlier grey-candidate study, at V0/V1/V2. One candidate (opt_q100_step2_try0_r12) was disqualified at all three grids on 'Cells with small determinant (<0.001)' (24-303 cells), a checkMesh failure the pre-registered profile does not waive; its coefficients are 5-8x the other two candidates' and are not usable. That leaves one valid pair: opt_q100_step0_try0 vs opt_q100_step2_try0. Stage T predicts step2 larger in both drag (2.231 -> 2.706) and downforce (1.078 -> 1.594); qualified Stage V agrees in direction at every one of the three grids for both responses. This is the opposite sign from the earlier grey-candidate finding (drag ranking inverted at every grid, 0.849/0.901/0.905 against Stage T's 2.582), and that inversion survives qualification unchanged, so the earlier negative result was a real observation about the wrong objects (non-binary designs whose 0.5 iso-surface did not match the object the Brinkman integral scored), not an artifact of an unqualified reference. This result is a positive signal, not proof: only one usable pair exists, the downforce margin (0.018-0.023) does not clear grid-to-grid drift (about 0.077), downforce itself is not grid-converged (the settling grid, V3 at ~1.28M cells, does not converge for this fixture), and iso-surface extraction loses 8-12% of design volume. The architecture's central assumption is not refuted and now has a positive signal, but is not yet demonstrated. P0 qualification remains No-Go.

disqualification.coefficient_inflation: Cd 6.63-8.68 and downforce 7.72-10.65 across V0-V2, roughly 5-8x the other two candidates' Cd (1.25-1.38) and clearly inflated on downforce too; not treated as trustworthy Stage V evidence.
disqualification.consequence: Only one candidate pair (opt_q100_step0_try0 vs opt_q100_step2_try0) remains usable. One of the two intended pair signs (a third, larger-volume-fraction candidate) does not exist as valid evidence.
disqualification.reason: Cells with small determinant (< 0.001), a checkMesh failure the pre-registered qualification profile does not waive (only 'Concave cells' is on the allowed-failure list).

extraction_volume_check.interpretation: step0/step2 are thin, roughly one-cell-thick bodies (design volume 0.05525 m^3 on a 0.05 m voxel grid) at ratio 0.88; the thicker, roughly two-cell-thick r12 body is closer at 0.92. This is a real extraction-defect signature (worse for thinner bodies), not a symptom of greyness -- these candidates are already binarized.
extraction_volume_check.statement: Iso-surface extraction loses volume relative to the thresholded design field for every candidate, including the disqualified one.

Cd.statement: Converges for both candidates: V1->V2 relative change is 1.13% (step0) and 1.30% (step2), under the pre-registered 2% relative cap.

downforce.statement: Does not converge: V0->V1 and V1->V2 changes are 0.072-0.078 for both candidates, against a 5e-3 absolute cap (Gate 3 fails at every transition).
downforce.statement_on_margin: The ranking margin (0.018-0.023) is smaller than each candidate's own grid-to-grid drift (about 0.072-0.078). Direction is consistent across all three grids; magnitude is not resolved against discretization uncertainty.

grid_convergence.stationarity_noise: Within-run stationarity noise (Cd_std, downforce_std across the qualification window) is of order 1e-6 to 1e-8 in all six qualified binarized runs -- negligible next to the 0.077 grid-to-grid drift. Discretization, not run-to-run noise, is the limiting factor.

v3_attempt.statement: V3 was not re-run for the binarized candidates. It is skipped on the basis of the qualified grey-candidate re-run (work/stage_sv_qualified_laminar/result_summary.json), where V3 at ~1.28M cells (candidate_a: 1,275,409 cells; candidate_b: 1,285,035 cells) hit the 500-iteration cap without meeting residualControl (U 1e-6, p 1e-5) for either candidate.
v3_attempt.statement_on_multiples: The p residual is 19-62x over its threshold at the 500-iteration cap; the U components range from about 16x (Ux, candidate A) to about 148x (Uy, candidate B) over their own threshold. Refused correctly as non-converged, not accepted at face value.

must_not_conclude.statement: This is a positive signal, not proof. The architecture's central assumption -- that the Stage T Brinkman surrogate preserves the body-fitted ranking -- is not refuted and now has a positive signal, but is not yet demonstrated.
what_would_settle_it: Rescue the mesh-disqualified candidate (opt_q100_step2_try0_r12) so a second independent pair sign exists.
Obtain candidate pairs whose ranking margin exceeds discretization uncertainty (currently the margin is smaller than the grid-to-grid drift).
Grid-converge the downforce response (V3 and beyond, or a formulation/mesh change that removes the current non-convergence at ~1.28M cells).

ranking_verdict.agreement: Qualified Stage V agrees with Stage T's direction (step2 > step0) at every one of the three grids, in both drag and downforce. This is the opposite sign from the earlier grey-candidate finding, where the analogous drag ranking (B/A) was inverted at every grid (0.849/0.901/0.905 against Stage T's 2.582) -- an inversion that survives qualification unchanged (see grey_candidate_reference below), so it was a real observation about the wrong objects, not an artifact of an unqualified reference.
ranking_verdict.caveat: This is a positive signal from one usable pair, not proof that the surrogate ranks correctly in general.
ranking_verdict.stage_t_direction: step2 > step0 in both drag (2.231 -> 2.706) and downforce (1.078 -> 1.594)

scope.model: one fixture, one flow condition (Re~300, laminar), one valid candidate pair, one machine (Apple M4, 32 GiB, Docker)

scope_limits: One usable candidate pair, not two: the third candidate (opt_q100_step2_try0_r12) was disqualified on checkMesh at all three grids and its coefficients are not evidence.

The ranking margin (downforce 0.018-0.023) does not clear discretization uncertainty (grid-to-grid drift about 0.077 for the same candidates). Direction agrees across all three grids; magnitude is unresolved.

Downforce is not grid-converged (Gate 3 fails, ~0.077 change against a 5e-3 absolute cap), and the grid that would settle it (V3, ~1.28M cells) does not converge for this fixture -- residuals stall 16-148x over their thresholds at the 500-iteration cap and are correctly refused, not the binarized candidates' own V3 (not run) but the qualified grey-candidate re-run at the same fixture and profile.
Cd does converge (V1->V2 about 1.1-1.3%, under the 2% cap), so the two responses are not equally resolved.

Iso-surface extraction loses volume (ratios 0.88, 0.88, 0.92 for one- to two-cell-thick bodies) -- a real extraction defect, not a greyness symptom, since all three candidates are genuinely binarized.
Within-run stationarity noise (~1e-6) is not the limiting factor; discretization is.
One fixture, one flow condition (Re~300 laminar), one valid candidate pair, one machine.
Not target-physics evidence, not benchmark evidence, qualifies no solver backend.

supersedes.reason: That test compared two non-binary grey Stage T candidates (peak rho 0.62 and 0.55, zero cells above 0.9) whose 0.5 iso-surface did not correspond to the object the Brinkman force integral scored (P2/P14). Its negative ranking result was a real observation about the wrong objects, not a test of the surrogate's fidelity as intended. This file repeats the same class of test on genuinely binarized candidates (RAMP-penalized interpolation, alphaMax lowered to the Brinkman saturation knee documented in problem_register P11, single Python ownership of projection, converged adjoints bound to a declared response, same-grid evaluation) against a qualified Stage V reference (checkMesh, explicit residualControl, force stationarity as hard gates).
